correctness.rationale: An incident pair has no completion and closes to E. A matching with at least four free vertices can avoid any particular residual edge by using different partners, whereas two free vertices force their joining edge. This gives the closed sets and the grading, including the missing cardinality n−1 rank. From each minimal nonclosed premise any sound basis must make its first strict addition using exactly that premise, since every proper subset is closed. The proposed rules add the entire required closure in one round (infeasible inputs contain an incident pair; the only other nonclosed inputs are near-perfect matchings). Every nonminimal nonclosed input contains an incident pair whose closure E is not contained in it, so it is not a pseudo-intent. Counting gives the stated optimum and ranks. The truncated Boolean recurrence gives μ(A,M)=(-1)^(r−1)(r−1), and combining the omitted near-perfect term m(2m−1)!! with the perfect term yields the signed full matching-count sum for −He_(2m)(1), also for m=2. For the simple-homotopy claim every lower fiber has greatest element B∖A; independently, in the residual face poset a near-perfect matching may be deleted by a simplicial collapse because its link is a cone on its unique perfect extension. The two wedge examples agree with the cited matching-complex computations. Verification caveat: verify.py line 115 reinstantiates the same seeded RNG for each draw, so the reported 15,000 additional K8 draws are repetitions of one mask, not diverse coverage. This does not affect the general proof, exhaustive K6 checks as coded, or the interval checks as coded; the uploaded script was inspected, not rerun.

value.rationale: The natural incidence context has an exact, simultaneously minimum and one-round implication basis, with a sharp lower bound even against iterative procedures. The interval identification imports more than Euler characteristics and the Hermite formula gives every top-interval Möbius number.
